title: Count thinning cannot separate anatomical and reconstruction dispersion under two equal-law models
abstract: We tested which count measurements can separate anatomical variation from reconstruction error. Two exact models have the same full observed count law: one has anatomical Fano factor 3, and one has Poisson anatomy with unbiased reconstruction loss. Detectors that share the reconstruction and artificial count thinning cannot separate these models. We derive an exact paired Pearson thinning identity and a calibrated count-contrast estimator for independent reconstructions. Shared reconstruction errors add an exact covariance bias. In 1,000 synthetic experiments with 2,000 independent edges, the independent-reconstruction estimator had mean 1.003 or 2.999 for the two anatomical models. With shared error fractions 0.25 and 0.5, Poisson anatomy gave estimates 1.501 and 1.998. Small-sample normal intervals under-covered. A separate exact example has bilateral conditional dispersion near 0.5 and Poisson marginal counts. Thus low bilateral dispersion alone does not establish sub-Poisson marginal counts. These are proofs and synthetic method checks, not new biological estimates. Calibration, fixed panel selection and conditional error independence are necessary. We supply proofs, code, an audit tool, aggregate results and reproduction steps.

display.caption: Exact thinning response and synthetic count estimates under two models with equal observed laws. Bars show simulation ranges. Shared reconstruction errors bias the cross estimate.
